topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture with a welcome and outlines the focus on the molecular mechanisms of inflammation initiation and resolution.

topics.label: Principles of Innate Immune Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core principles of innate immune recognition, including the essential features of PAMPs and DAMPs and the cellular localization of pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific PRR families, their downstream intracellular signaling pathways, and the assembly of the inflammasome complex.

topics.label: Sentinel Cell Activation and Leukocyte Extravasation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated sentinel cells and endothelial adhesion molecules coordinate the recruitment, rolling, and extravasation of circulating leukocytes into inflamed tissues.

topics.label: Lymphatic Drainage and Antigen Transport
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how lymphatic drainage transports fluid and activated dendritic cells from inflamed tissues to lymph nodes to prime adaptive immune responses.

topics.label: Systemic Inflammatory Pathology and Septic Shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic discusses the severe pathological consequences of excessive systemic cytokine production, leading to loss of blood pressure and septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms required to terminate inflammation, restore damaged tissue via repair processes, and manage persistent stimuli through chronic responses like granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the complement system.
